question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 154 and 7 respectively. If one of the numbers is 77, then find the other number.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the standard property: **Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF**

Let the unknown number be x.

77 × x = 154 × 7

x = (154 ÷ 77) × 7

x = 2 × 7 = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of two numbers = 154

HCF of two numbers = 7

First number (A) = 77

**Formula Used:**

For any two positive integers A and B:

A × B = LCM(A, B) × HCF(A, B)

**Calculations:**

Let the second number be B.

⇒ 77 × B = 154 × 7

⇒ B = (154 × 7) ÷ 77

⇒ B = 154 ÷ 77 × 7

⇒ B = 2 × 7

⇒ B = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF of Fractions

LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).
HCF of fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators).

Co-prime Numbers Property

If two numbers are co-prime (their HCF is 1), then their LCM is always equal to their product.

Product Rule Limitation

The mathematical rule (Product of numbers = LCM × HCF) is valid ONLY for exactly two numbers. It cannot be applied to three or more numbers.
